title: Anomaly Hunting Dashboard - sketches and investigation stories
content:
Purpose:
This working doc collects sketches and short investigation stories for a unified ‘Anomaly Hunting’ dashboard inside Console. Focus: help engineers and on-call SREs find subtle signal in noisy failure modes (timeouts, 5xx, and model-level decoding anomalies) and quickly form testable hypotheses and remediation actions.

Why another view?
- Current triage flows are either too coarse (aggregate error counts) or too low-level (raw traces). We need a middle ground: session- and hypothesis-oriented views tailored for model inference errors.
- Prior docs cover error cards and timeline playback; this is more investigative: heatmaps, token waterfalls, synthetic replays, automated hypothesis extraction, and backlog-ready stories.

Primary goals (MVP):
1) Rapidly surface sessions with anomalous model output characteristics (repetition loops, hallucination-like token patterns, unexpected eos timing).
2) Combine system signals (latency, 5xx, infra tags) with model signals (log prob dips, token-entropy spike) in a single timeline.
3) Provide quick actions: snapshot-to-replay, pin prompt & seed, mutate model variant, and open ticket prefilled with artifacts.

Personas:
- On-call SRE (latency/5xx first)
- ML infra engineer (model decode and quantization artifacts)
- Product engineer (customer-reported bad outputs)

High-level flow (detect -> contain -> investigate -> remediate):
1) Detect: anomaly detector flags a cohort (e.g., 10% of requests have token-entropy > 5 sigma).
2) Contain: auto-sample representative sessions and surface a severity score and impacted routes.
3) Investigate: deep view with token waterfall, per-token timing, system spans, and request metadata.
4) Remediate: quick actions (rollback to known-good model, increase kv cache TTL, bump timeout, schedule canary test).

Key components (wireframe notes):
- Top banner: cohort summary (metric deltas, affected models/routes, severity) + quick actions (snapshot, rollback, create-ticket).
- Left column: session list (compact rows) with: request id, user route, latency, status, severity, tiny sparkline of "token entropy". Click to open session.
- Main pane: session canvas with synchronized timelines:
  - Model-decoding waterfall: tokens stacked horizontally, colored by token log-prob percentile (red = low prob), annotations for repetition or EOS gaps.
  - Per-token timing bar: microseconds/ms for each token generation; vertical lines for notable spikes.
  - System span strip: backend latency, vGPU queue time, network hops.
  - Prompt & metadata: prompt truncated preview, prompt-tokens hashed to anonymize PII, customer route, model variant, quantization profile.
- Right rail: automated hypotheses + suggested next actions: root-cause candidates (e.g., kernel mismatch, bad prompt formatting, reduced kv cache), with confidence score and short justification.
- Bottom: related sessions cluster map (similar token patterns) and a mini-replay player (step through tokens at 1x/0.5x/2x speed).

Sketch details (ASCII-like description for designer/dev):
[Top banner] | Severity 8.2 | +340% token-entropy | Model: redwood/4x-quant | Actions: [Snapshot] [Rollback] [Open ticket]
[Left col] Session list: 
  * rq_9b2f  | /chat/send | 1.2s | 5xx | sev7 | sparkline ▉▅▃▂▁
  * rq_3c88  | /embed    | 0.12s| ok  | sev2 | sparkline ▇▇▇▇

[Main pane] Timeline (time axis left->right)
  Token waterfall (color-coded): "Hello"(green) "world"(amber) "..."(red-lowprob)
  Token timing: |__|____|________|  (ms bars)
  System spans: [router]---[gpu-queue]-----[infer]--[postproc]

Right rail: Auto-hypotheses
  1) "Quantization boundary artifacts" (confidence 0.62) — explanation: low log-probs on subword ids 434-440 repeated; suggested: test without 8-bit quantized kernel
  2) "Late EOS due to prompt-template" (confidence 0.35) — explanation: prompt ends with open code fence; suggested: try prompt-sanitizer

Investigation stories (short scenarios used in grooming/testing):
- Story A (SRE): spike of 5xx + high token-entropy for /chat/send. User visible. Using dashboard, SRE notices GPU queue time increased; token timing normal. Hypothesis: router overload -> enqueueing caused timeouts. Action: enable burst autoscale on dedicated pool.
- Story B (ML infra): low-prob token streaks on model variant v2-quant. Debug: switch to v2-fp16 in replay; issue disappears. Create MR to add quantization test harness to CI.
- Story C (Product): customer reports hallucination. Dashboard shows repetition loop starting at token 112 with log-prob collapse. Right-rail suggests prompt-truncation edge-case. Suggested quick win: prompt sanitizer in front of route and schedule canary of sanitized prompts.

Backlog (prioritized, groomed into tickets):
- AH-101: UI shell + session list + cohort banner (M0) — acceptance: filter by model, route, severity; snapshot action saves artifacts to ticket template.
- AH-102: Token waterfall + per-token log-prob visualization (M1) — acceptance: color by percentile, hover shows raw log-prob and token id.
- AH-103: Synchronized system spans overlay (M1) — acceptance: show backend spans and link to tracing trace id.
- AH-104: Automated hypothesis engine (prototype) (M2) — acceptance: surface top-3 hypotheses with confidence and rationale, link to deterministic checks.
- AH-105: Synthetic replay harness & mutation controls (M2) — acceptance: run local replay with model variant selector and prompt mutations.

Metrics & success criteria:
- Time to actionable hypothesis: reduce from median 26m -> <8m for P1 anomalies.
- Ticket prefill ratio: % of auto-created tickets with snapshot + replication steps >= 80%.
- Mean time from detection to rollback (when needed) < 15m for infra-caused P1.

Privacy & security notes:
- Prompts must be hashed/anonymized by default. Provide an explicit "reveal" action gated by user perms + audit log.
- Snapshot export should strip any customer PII and include only token ids and truncated prompt unless user explicitly opt-in.

Design tradeoffs we debated:
- Live per-token log-probs vs sampled heatmap: live is powerful but noisy and expensive for high-throughput cohorts. Compromise: sample up to N tokens per session for the waterfall; provide full dump in snapshot.
- Auto-hypothesis confidence: start with rule-based heuristics (entropy spikes, repetition detection, quantization table mismatches) before ML models. Easier to audit and explain.

Open questions:
- What thresholding should detection use for "anomalous token entropy"? (Diego to prototype with synthetic replay data)
- How to surface hardware-specific kernel mismatch warnings without exposing vendor internals? (security follow-up with infra)
- Should replay be run against customer-provided keys/credentials in private deployments? (legal + security)

Next steps (for this doc):
- Design: create low-fi Figma screens for top banner, session canvas, and right-rail hypotheses (assigned: Priya)
- Engineering: spike a lightweight token-log-prob sampler pipeline (assigned: Samir)
- SRE: populate detection ruleset with two simple heuristics (latency+entropy) and run on last 7 days (assigned: Diego)

Notes to self / quick todos:
- Add example screenshots from production incidents (anonymized)
- Draft acceptance test checklist for AH-102 (token hover, color legend, percentile bins)
- Cross-link to incident playbook for rollback actions

References and inspiration:
- existing failure timeline and replay docs (see linked artifacts)
- internal paper: "Token-level diagnostics for production LLMs" (private internal draft)

This is intentionally work-in-progress. Use this doc as the canonical place for short investigation stories and wireframe fragments until we create a fuller PRD.

End of doc.
